covert

KOH-vurt — rhymes with 'over' plus a 't'; a covert operation stays quietly 'covered' from view. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Covert is secret or not openly displayed.

The company launched a covert investigation into the missing funds without alerting any employees.

Example

A store manager suspects an employee of theft. Instead of confronting him directly, her approach stays covert: she quietly reviews security footage after hours and asks a trusted coworker to keep an unannounced eye on the register, all without the suspect ever knowing he's being watched.

Everything is done secretly, without anyone knowing it's happening. Unlike 'obvious,' which is easy to notice, covert means deliberately hidden from view.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

secret: Secret is the plain, everyday word for anything kept hidden from others. Covert is the more official cousin: a covert operation or investigation is deliberately concealed as a matter of strategy, usually by a government or company, not just something one person keeps quiet.

clandestine: Clandestine means done in secrecy, and it usually hints the hidden activity is illicit or forbidden — a clandestine meeting breaks some rule. Covert carries no such judgment: a covert program can be fully approved and legal, simply not displayed openly.

undercover: Undercover describes a person working in disguise to gather information — an undercover officer lives out a false identity. Covert describes the operation or program itself being hidden, not the assumed role of one person.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

overt: done openly, not hidden

public: open and known to everyone

Where it sits · how deliberately something is kept hidden

quiet → covert → top-secret

quiet vs. covert: Quiet is weaker than covert — something quiet just avoids drawing attention, while covert is deliberately kept secret and hidden from view.

top-secret vs. covert: Top-secret is stronger than covert — a covert program is deliberately kept out of open view, but something top-secret is so tightly hidden that even knowing it exists is restricted to a cleared few.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — covert-: covered, hidden (Old French/Latin (cooperire, 'to cover completely'))

Put it together: Covert comes from Old French covert, the past participle of covrir ('to cover'), itself from Latin cooperire. At its root, something covert is simply kept 'covered' from view.

Use the root in a new word: discover: In the old photograph, every farmhand at the long table wears a bright kerchief.
